summary: Cambria County tower built in 1921 and raised to 86 feet in 1939; a 2011 blog post says it was still there, and no later source confirms its condition.

facts.status_note: A 2011 local history post says the tower was still there; no later source we read confirms its condition.

events.note: Completed by early August 1921 on the land of Johnstown attorney F.P. Martin, per 1921 newspapers
Towerman John Vasil, Jr., reported the season's first call from the tower in October 1921

evidence.supports: State Department of Forestry, district forester's report, July 1921
evidence.quote: to the State Department of Forestry

evidence.supports: Tower to go up on the property of attorney F.P. Martin and be rushed to completion
evidence.quote: Erection of the first tower in Lower Yoder township on the property of Attorney F.P. Martin of Johnstown will be rushed to completion as rapidly as possible.

evidence.supports: Telephone line to each tower so towermen could alert fire wardens
evidence.quote: A telephone line will also be run to each tower so that the towerman can notify fire wardens promptly at the first indication of flames.

evidence.supports: Lower Yoder named among the first 18 towers to be put up
evidence.quote: One of the first 18 towers will be put up at Lower Yoder, Cambria county.

evidence.supports: Tower 60 feet high on the highest point in the Johnstown section, completed, view of more than 20 miles
evidence.quote: Lower Yoder Fire Observation tower, 60 feet high, situated on the highest point in the Johnstown section, at an elevation of over 2700 feet, and commanding a view of more than 20 miles has been completed.

evidence.supports: First of four towers planned for the Gallitzin district
evidence.quote: The tower is the first of four to be built in the Gallitzin district.

evidence.supports: First call of the 1921 season came from towerman John Vasil, Jr., on the Lower Yoder tower
evidence.quote: The first call of the season from the towers came into the Johnstown office from Towerman John Vasil, Jr., on the Lower Yoder tower shortly after noon last Saturday.

evidence.supports: The October 1921 smoke was not a real forest fire
evidence.quote: his investigation showed that this smoke did not come from a real forest fire

evidence.supports: Newspaper said the response showed fires would be attacked within an hour of discovery
evidence.quote: such fires will be attacked within an hour after they are discovered

evidence.supports: Tower raised from sixty to eighty-six feet in June 1939
evidence.quote: The tower at Lower Yoder has been raised in height from sixty-feet to eighty-six feet.

evidence.supports: Blog says the tower was still there in 2011
Generations of children enjoyed the view from the tower off Decker Avenue, Lower Yoder Township
evidence.quote: Generations of kids have taken in the view at the Fire Tower - off of Decker Avenue in Lower Yoder Township.

evidence.supports: Author says the thought of the climb makes their legs shake
evidence.quote: Just thinking about walking up to the top makes my legs shake.

sources.title: Vintage Johnstown: Fire Tower - Decker Avenue - Lower Yoder

notes_for_editor: The 1921 and 1939 history comes from newspaper extracts on the eastern lookouts page; we did not check the originals. The newest status evidence is a May 2011 blog post saying the tower was still there. No source after 2011 gives its condition, ownership or access. Map databases (TopoQuest, anyplaceamerica) list a 'Lower Yoder Fire Tower' near the same coordinates at about 2,673 ft, but a map listing does not show whether the structure stands. The record's height_m is 26.2 m, the 1939 figure.
